model_architecture: TF-IDF (1-2 word n-grams, sublinear_tf) + Calibrated Logistic Regression (Platt scaling)

cross_split_similarity_diagnostics.methodology: TF-IDF Sublinear Vectorization with Cosine Similarity. Target splits evaluate maximum nearest-neighbor similarity against reference split.
cross_split_similarity_diagnostics.threshold_and_limitations: LIMITATION AND INTERPRETATION NOTICE: Lexical and n-gram similarity measures shared institutional and conversational vocabulary inherent to telephony dialogues (e.g. greetings, institutional names, telecom/banking terminology). A high or moderate similarity score alone neither proves nor disproves data leakage. True data leakage is strictly evaluated through: (1) scenario-family isolation, (2) exact dialogue text hash overlap, and (3) conversation ID partitioning, all of which are verified at exactly 0% overlap.

synthetic_dataset_limitations.synthetic_provenance: Evaluated strictly on synthetic domain scenario transcripts (KAVACH synthetic v2).
synthetic_dataset_limitations.telephony_generalization_limit: Does not establish or claim production telephony accuracy in unconstrained real-world environments with telephony noise, accent variation, or live audio artifacts.
synthetic_dataset_limitations.leakage_isolation: Strict 0% scenario-family, 0% exact dialogue hash, and 0% CID leakage across train, val, and test splits.

disclaimer: Metrics measured strictly on held-out synthetic domain scenario test set. Real-world wild telephony performance requires field validation.
